{{Quote|Energize the shields!|General Ceel giving commands during the Battle of Naboo|<ref name="Junior">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' junior novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Tobler Ceel''' was an [[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as a [[General/Legends|general]] in the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]]. During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Gungans were driven from their [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], leading Ceel to begin planning reprisal attacks. Ultimately, the Gungans allied with [[Human/Legends|Humans]] to retake Naboo, forming a plan in which the Gungan Grand Army marched toward the city of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] as a diversion. Ceel led the [[Army/Legends|army]] on the march alongside [[Bombad General/Legends|Bombad General]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]] south of Theed, the Gungans met the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] in [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|battle]].

General Ceel gave the orders to raise the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], which blocked the Trade Federation's [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]]. However, the Trade Federation's [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] were able to get through the [[Force field/Legends|force field]], and Ceel ordered counterattacks to keep the shields safe. The Gungan also signaled the order for retreat from the overwhelming battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] once the shields were destroyed but was taken [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] along with the other Gungan [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanding officers]]. The battle was unexpectedly won for the Gungans when the destruction of a [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] shut down every battle droid on the plains, and Ceel later led a victory procession of Gungans in a celebration held in Theed.

==Biography==
===The Invasion of Naboo===
{{Quote|Gungans no dyin' witout a fight. Wesa warriors. Wesa got a grand army.|Jar Jar Binks|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:Naboo_Swamp_Battle.jpg|thumb|right|250px|After the Trade Federation attacked the Gungans, General Ceel began planning guerilla attacks in reprisal.]]
Tobler Ceel, an [[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]]<ref name="Collection" /> [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]]<ref name="TPM novel" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]],<ref name="Collection2" /> was [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]] of the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]],<ref name="TPM novel" /> in which he<ref name="Collection2" /> held the rank of [[General/Legends|general]].<ref name="TPM novel" /> To keep the [[Army/Legends|army's]] [[Militiagung/Legends|militiagungs]] in full form, Ceel established a [[Scrumma Jawbone training center|training center]] in the [[Scrumma Jawbone]], an arm of [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]]. There, militiagungs could practice using projectile weapons, such as the [[arbalest]], [[Atlatl/Legends|atlatl]], and [[Cesta/Legends|cesta]].<ref name="Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Naboo was [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invaded]] by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], who, after occupying the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], turned their attention to [[Death/Legends|pacifying]] the Gungans to prevent any reprisal attacks. The Trade Federation discovered the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] Gungan capital city of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]] and [[Siege of Otoh Gunga|drove]] the inhabitants out, although many were able to escape in a mass evacuation and rally at their [[Gungan Sacred Place/Legends|Sacred Place]]. The Gungan military leadership, including General Ceel and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]], immediately began planning retaliatory attacks. Their plans involved strategic [[Guerrilla warfare/Legends|guerilla warfare]] raids on Trade Federation forces, where Gungans would perform hit-and-runs before disappearing into the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]].<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

Ceel's plans went unfulfilled when the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen of Naboo]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], formed an alliance with the Gungan leader, [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]]. The Gungans and Humans planned to retake their planet by amassing the Gungan Grand Army on a march toward Theed as a diversion while the Naboo infiltrated the capital.<ref name="GB" /> Ceel knew that the Gungans would need to make use of their [[Fambaa/Legends|fambaa]]-mounted [[Deflector shield/Legends|energy shields]] to withstand the Trade Federation's [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]]. His plan was to force the Trade Federation [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] into close-quarters combat, where the Gungans stood a better chance of defeating them or could at least hold them off until Queen Amidala captured the [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]].<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile|47|GUN 5-6|Gungan Energy Shield}}</ref>

===Riding to battle===
{{Quote|Wesa ready to do our-sa part.|Boss Rugor Nass, speaking of the Gungan Grand Army|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:Gungan_Grand_Army.jpg|thumb|left|300px|General Ceel led the Gungan Grand Army in their march to battle against the Trade Federation.]]
Ceel rode at the front of the army as its leader along with the new [[Bombad General/Legends|Bombad General]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], who had been personally promoted by Nass. Ceel disapproved of Binks' promotion, giving him no practical responsibilities in the army other than to set an example by dying well.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Ceel had hoped to position the army atop [[Shaak Ridge/Legends|Shaak Ridge]] south of Theed, using the high ground as a vantage point to decimate the Trade Federation machinery with [[Gungan catapult/Legends|energy catapults]] and [[Sniper/Legends|snipers]] wielding atlatls and cestas. However, the Trade Federation anticipated the Gungans procession early and claimed the Ridge first, which was discovered by [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] under Ceel's command after the Gungan Grand Army arrived at the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]]. The general was disappointed in the lack of strategic maneuverability, but he knew that the plains' proximity to the [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] would allow the Gungans to make a quick retreat if necessary.<ref name="GB" />

Riding a [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]] at the head of the army alongside his command unit, General Ceel<ref name="TPM novel" /> and Captain Tarpals<ref name="TPM" /> personally [[Limb/Legends|hand]]-signaled the [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to halt. Ceel<ref name="TPM novel" /> and Tarpals<ref name="TPM" /> ordered the activation of the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]], covering the whole army in a [[Force field/Legends|force field]]. On the orders of the [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM command battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]], the Trade Federation [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]] fired on the shield, but found it to be impregnable, causing the Gungans to cheer. In response, OOM-9 ordered the [[Tank/Legends|tanks]] to cease firing, and the Trade Federation began unloading B1-Series [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] from their [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transports]], which caused concern among Ceel and the other Gungan [[Commander/Legends|commanders]].<ref name="TPM novel" />

===Victory from the jaws of defeat===
{{Quote|Disen very bombad.''"<br />"''Me hope dis worken for da Queen.|Jar Jar Binks and Tobler Ceel, while taken prisoner in the Battle of Naboo|<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
[[File:Gungan_Shield.png|thumb|right|350px|On the Great Grass Plains, Ceel ordered the raising of the Fambaa shield generators and prioritized their defense.]]
The battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were able to pass through the shields and begin firing on the Gungans,<ref name="TPM novel" /> which prompted Ceel to order his militiagungs to counterattack with atlatls, cestas,<ref name="GB" /> and [[Electropole/Legends|electropoles]].<ref name="Junior" /> Multiple waves of battle droids were destroyed,<ref name="GB" /> but as the fighting escalated, Ceel tightened his forces around the shield generators, aware of the danger the Trade Federation tanks would pose if they could strike the Gungan army. The fighting grew so intense that the general had to commit all of his reserve troops. Eventually, [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] breached the force field and destroyed the shield generators, opening up the Gungans to tank fire. Ceel realized that the battle had been lost and signaled for the retreat to the swamps.<ref name="TPM novel" />

A majority of the Gungans were not able to escape, including the general, who was taken [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]] on the battlefield and held near the other [[Commanding officer/Legends|officers]], including Binks. Ceel and Binks expressed concern about their situation, hoping that Amidala's plan had still been successful. The Gungans were unexpectedly saved when the [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] destroyed the Trade Federation's [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']]. The loss of the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] quickly deactivated every battle droid on the Great Grass Plains.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The Gungans realized their seemingly impossible victory and cheered,<ref name="TPM" /> and Ceel and Binks would later lead the Gungans on kaadu in a celebration of Naboo's freedom in Theed.<ref name="TPM novel" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Retreat!|General Ceel's orders during the Battle of Naboo|<ref name="Junior" />}}
[[File:General_Jar_Jar.png|thumb|left|300px|Tobler Ceel disapproved of Jar Jar Binks' (pictured) promotion to general.]]
Shortly after the Trade Federation's attacks on the Gungans, Ceel began planning retribution against the Trade Federation.<ref name="GB" /> He grunted sourly after learning of Binks' promotion in the army and unwillingly accepted him into his officer's council, telling the notoriously clumsy Gungan to die well. In the Battle of Naboo, Ceel was worried when the Trade Federation began to unload its battle droids, and urged his troops to fight on as the fighting grew intense.<ref name="TPM novel" /> He was quick to realize when the Gungans were overrun but was still reluctant when he ordered a retreat.<ref name="GB" /> He was forlorn when he was captured by the Trade Federation, worried about the outcome of Amidala's plan.<ref name="TPM novel" /> After the battle, he did not believe that it had been a stirring victory for the Gungans, while all of his people were still proud of their efforts.<ref name="GB" /> Ceel had [[Color/Legends|yellow]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and purple and white skin.<ref name="Collection" /> In Gungan culture, Ceel's first name of Tobler meant "laughs easily" and his surname meant "vigilant sentry."<ref name="GCG">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|Shoota' them up real good!|General Tobler Ceel|<ref name="Collection" />}}
As a high-ranking<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|113|Ceel, General Tobler}}</ref> career [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the Gungan Grand Army,<ref name="TPM novel" /> Tobler Ceel had a tactical mind, crafting multiple strategies during the Invasion of Naboo to protect his people.<ref name="GB" /> In his capacity as a general, Ceel wielded command over the entire Gungan Grand Army, and was responsible for directing its movements during the Battle of Naboo.<ref name="TPM novel" />

==Equipment==
During the Battle of the Great Grass Plains, Ceel wore brown sleeveless [[Armor/Legends|armor]] with grey [[Clothing/Legends|pants]], along with brown [[Gauntlet/Legends|gauntlets]]. In the battle,<ref name="Collection2" /> and the celebration held at the end of the invasion, Ceel rode atop a kaadu.<ref name="TPM novel" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''The Phantom Menace'' drafts===
{{Quote|Their heavy armor will come through first. Position the disrupter rays to knock out the gravity pulses.|General Ceel in the revised rough draft of ''The Phantom Menace''|<ref name="Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref>}}
[[File:EPI_TPM_poster.png|thumb|right|200px|Tobler Ceel was present in the screenplay drafts for ''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' (poster pictured).]]
General Ceel was present in director [[George Lucas]]' drafts of the [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> which premiered on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Ceel was present in several scenes in the revised rough draft of the film's screenplay. One early scene was set in a Gungan war room prior to the Battle of Naboo, where Ceel, identified as the highest ranking general in the Gungan Grand Army, reports that he can commit three hundred [[Battalion/Legends|battalions]] to the battle.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> 

In a later scene where the Gungans wait at the edge of the swamps prior to the battle, a Gungan general named [[Yoss]] warns that the army should should move into the plains to prevent the Trade Federation from destroying the swamps, but Ceel maintains that the Gungans should wait until the energy shields have been raised. Later, as the Trade Federation battle droids penetrate the Gungan shields, Ceel confirms to his troops that the droid's heavy armor will pierce the shields first, and that they need to use [[disrupter ray]]s on their [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] pulses, which causes the Trade Federation's Armored Assault Tanks to crash. Later, the Gungans wait underwater until they receive a [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]] of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]], at which point, Ceel orders Binks to take their troops to the surface. These scenes were not included in the final draft of the screenplay, which still featured Ceel commanding the Gungan Grand Army during the Battle of Naboo.<ref name="Insider's Guide" />

At one point in production, visual effects artist [[Dennis Muren]] supervised a shot where he chose to place the camera at a low angle to present Ceel and the Gungan Grand Army in a heroic light, which was inspired by the cinematography of films by director [[Wikipedia:John Ford|John Ford]].<ref name="Star News">{{InsiderCite|47|Star News}}</ref> Ultimately, General Ceel was not included in the finished film, with [[Holocron continuity database]] manager [[Leland Chee]] confirming his lines were spoken by Captain Tarpals instead.<ref name="chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=01515#16873740|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2007-08-30|time=2:06 PM|quote=Tobler Ceel has never been confirmed as appearing in The Phantom Menace. The lines from the published script attributed to Ceel are spoken by Captain Tarpals in the film.}}</ref> 

===Adaptations and other appearances===
[[File:S3_-_General_Ceel.png|thumb|left|250px|General Ceel's role in ''The Phantom Menace'' was taken by Captain Tarpals, and his likeness in ''Star Wars: Force Collection'' (pictured) was a repurposed image of Tarpals.]]
Ceel appeared in several adaptations of ''The Phantom Menace'', which include some of his scenes from the final screenplay.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> He first appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] of ''The Phantom Menace'' by [[Terry Brooks]],<ref name="TPM novel" /> released on [[April 21]], 1999<ref name="Noveldate">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> and also appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] by [[Patricia C. Wrede]],<ref name="Junior" /> and the [[Mighty Chronicles]] [[The Phantom Menace (Mighty Chronicles)|adaptation]] by [[John Whitman]],<ref name="Mighty">[[The Phantom Menace (Mighty Chronicles)|''The Phantom Menace'' Mighty Chronicles adaptation]]</ref> both of which were released in [[May]] 1999.<ref name="Juniordate">{{CollectorCite|6|The Padawan Reading List}}</ref><ref name="MightyChronicles date">{{Chronicle|old=1|url=cgi-bin/Adult/view.cgi?isbn=0811823156|text=Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace}}</ref> Each of those sources include Ceel's role in the battle, and Tarpals is not present.<ref name="TPM novel" /><ref name="Junior" /><ref name="Mighty" /> In Brooks' novel, Ceel is confused by the deactivation of the battle droids at the end of the Battle of Naboo and urges Binks to investigate by touching one,<ref name="TPM novel" /> which differs from the film version, in which Tarpals immediately recognizes that the control ship has been destroyed and pushes a nearby droid over, an action Binks repeats.<ref name="TPM" />

Ceel's full name was first given in the CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide]]'',<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> released on [[June 23]], 1999,<ref name="Insider guide date">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news19990623.html|text=''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''Insider's Guide''}}</ref> which provided details about his appearances in the revised rough draft of ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> The full name was then used in the [[2000]] [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook|Core Rulebook]] for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' as an example of a Gungan name.<ref name="Roleplaying">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref> In the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', Ceel's name could be randomly selected as a Gungan leader in the standard game mode.<ref name="GB" /> The character was first visually depicted in the [[2013]] mobile game ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="Collection2" /> which used an [[:File:GeneralTarpals-SWE.png|image]] of Tarpals taken from the [[2005]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''</ref> to represent Ceel.<ref name="Collection2" />
